questions.question: A shop buys batches of $y$ units at a constant unit price $c$ per unit, and demand occurs at a constant rate $D$ units per day. Which expression gives the purchasing cost of one batch?
For an inventory policy with unit price $c$ and demand rate $D$, the long-run purchasing cost rate is $cD$. Which conditions does this formula rely on?
options: A constant batch size, and orders at zero stock
No fixed order charge, and no stock at the end
A constant unit price, and all demand is met
Equal spacing of orders, and instant delivery

questions.question: A shop pays a unit price $c$ per unit and a fixed charge $K$ per order, meets demand $D$ per day in full and places $\frac{D}{y}$ orders per day with batch size $y$. What happens to the purchasing cost rate $cD$ and the fixed-charge rate $\frac{KD}{y}$ when $y$ is doubled?
options: $cD$ and $\frac{KD}{y}$ both halve, as orders are rarer.
$cD$ doubles with the batch, while $\frac{KD}{y}$ halves.
$cD$ and $\frac{KD}{y}$ both stay the same, as $D$ is fixed.
$cD$ stays the same, while $\frac{KD}{y}$ falls by half.

questions.question: When choosing the batch size $y$ for a policy with constant unit price $c$ and demand rate $D$ met in full, the term $cD$ is often left out of the cost rate that is compared across batch sizes. Why does this not change the best $y$?
options: $cD$ is usually small compared with the other costs.
$cD$ is equal for all $y$ and shifts every cost alike.
$cD$ is paid only once, when the first order is placed.
$cD$ is already included in the fixed charge per order.

questions.question: The unit price $c$ is measured in euros per unit and the demand rate $D$ in units per week. In which unit is the purchasing cost rate $cD$ expressed?
A café buys coffee at a constant price $c=4$ euros per kg, in batches of $y=120$ kg, and meets all demand of $D=15$ kg per day. What is its long-run purchasing cost rate?
A shop meets all demand of 120 units per week for a part bought at a constant price of 2.50 euros per unit, in batches of 400 units. What is the purchasing cost per 52-week year?
A shop orders batches of $y=200$ units at a constant price of 3 euros per unit and meets all demand of 50 units per day. What is the purchasing cost of one order?
A graph of cumulative purchasing cost against time is a straight line rising from 0 to 9000 euros over 30 days. The unit price is constant at 15 euros and all demand is met. What is the demand rate?

A shop meets all demand of 20 units per day at a constant price of 5 euros per unit. It compares a policy with batches of 100 units and one with batches of 400 units. What purchasing cost rates do the two policies have?

Each order of $y$ units costs $cy$ at a constant unit price $c$, and with demand rate $D$ met in full one order is placed every $\frac{y}{D}$ time units. How does the long-run purchasing cost rate follow from these two facts?

A supplier charges 20 euros per unit for orders below 100 units and 18 euros per unit for orders of 100 units or more, on every unit of the order. Demand $D$ is met in full. Why can purchasing cost no longer be left out when choosing the batch size $y$?
options: Its rate, $20D$ or $18D$, now depends on the choice of $y$.
It still can, because all demand is met at the same rate $D$.
It must be included because it is the largest cost component.
It must be included, but only for batches below 100 units.

questions.question: A planner looks for the batch size with the lowest cost rate of all costs except purchasing and finds $y=40$, with cost rate 50 euros per day. The unit price is constant at 6 euros and demand of 25 units per day is met in full. Which statement about the policy with the lowest full cost rate is correct?
options: It is still $y=40$, with full cost rate 50 euros per day.
It has a larger $y$, as purchasing favours bigger batches.
It is still $y=40$, with full cost rate 200 euros per day.
It is still $y=40$, with full cost rate 290 euros per day.

questions.question: A bakery buys eggs at a constant price of 18 euros per dozen and meets all demand of 30 eggs per day. What is its purchasing cost rate?
A shop meets all demand of 30 units per day. The unit price is 8 euros for the first 20 days and 10 euros from day 20 on. What is the total purchasing cost over the first 50 days?

A shop meets all demand of 40 units per day. The unit price is 5 euros, or 4.80 euros on every unit of an order of at least 100 units. The shop orders 80 units at a time. How does its purchasing cost rate change if it orders 100 units at a time instead?
options: It falls by 20 euros per day.
It falls by 8 euros per day.
It rises by 100 euros per day.
It stays the same, since demand is unchanged.

questions.question: A product has constant unit price $c$ and demand rate $D$. Policy A meets all demand from stock; policy B lets customers wait and fills all their orders at the next delivery; policy C turns 10% of customers away. Which policies have long-run purchasing cost rate $cD$?
options: Only A: waiting customers lower the purchasing rate.
All three: the unit price is the same in each policy.
A and C: only B changes when the units are bought.
A and B: each buys every unit demanded, B later.

questions.question: A manager argues that small batches are cheaper to buy: at a constant unit price $c$, an order of 50 units costs $50c$ while one of 200 units costs $200c$. Demand $D$ is met in full either way. What is wrong with this argument?
options: Nothing: the purchasing cost per day falls with $y$.
Small orders recur more often; both rates are $cD$.
Large orders get a lower price, so 200 is cheaper.
The purchasing cost per day is $cy$, not per order.

questions.question: Demand of 10 units per day is met in full. Policy A orders 40 units at 30 euros per unit and has 50 euros per day of all other costs. Policy B orders 100 units at a qualifying price of 28 euros per unit and has 85 euros per day of all other costs. Which policy has the lower full cost rate, and by how much?

A shop meets all demand of 100 units per week and orders $y$ units at a time. Supplier X charges 10 euros per unit plus 50 euros per order; supplier Y charges 10.20 euros per unit and nothing per order. For which batch sizes is X cheaper in purchasing plus order charges per week?
options: For no batch size, as X adds an order fee
For every batch size, as X's unit price is lower
